- A changelog section is `## {version}`, a date and compare-link line, then Major, Minor and Patch Changes groups (`[changelog] layout = "grouped"`, the default), or the heading and one bullet list (`"flat"`). `render_section` is pure: the planner puts the layout, the UTC date and the link in `ChangelogInput::style`, and the link needs a GitHub repository (`[release] forge-repository`, else the `origin` remote) plus a tag on the previous version. Readers (`find_section`, `has_heading`, release notes) key on the `## {version}` line only, so they read both layouts; a fixed group's release notes file each member's entries under the bump group the member recorded them in.

It never observes a registry or the forge, so the checks that need one (a published version left behind, a name another project owns) are left to the release itself; a refusal becomes a `Stop` finding. `publish.versionedOnly` (optional, absent when empty) names the bumped packages with no publish target, such as a private fixed-group member, which are versioned but never published; the PR body lists them after the publish table. Rows are keyed by the qualified release identity, so `cargo/x` and `npm/x` stay apart.
- `changed_source_files_since_last_tag` lists, per package, the files that differ from its last tag after dropping `DEFAULT_IGNORED_PATHS` (tests, benches, examples, snapshots, Markdown), and `uncovered_changes` returns the changed packages that no pending changeset, nor any member of their fixed or linked group, covers. `unreleased_changes` builds `ReleasePreview.unreleased` from them, so the PR body lists the packages they find.

## Idempotent apply

A crash or a failed lockfile refresh can stop apply after some files are written. Applying the same plan again is file-level idempotent, and a fresh run recovers that plan from a checkpoint ([ADR 13](../adr/0013-interrupted-version-runs-resume-from-a-checkpoint-ref.md)):

- Before its first write, `version` records `HEAD`, the index and the workspace's working tree (untracked files included) as a commit at `refs/worktree/callisto/checkpoint/version`, with `HEAD`, a digest of the tags and the Callisto version in its message (`GitAccess::create_checkpoint`, through `CommandRunner::run_with_env` and a temporary index). It is created only if absent (E341), never signed, and deleted after the last effect, including the emitted decision and preview.
- A run that finds the checkpoint checks it out in a temporary worktree (with `HEAD` on the commit the run started from, so commit inference reads real history), loads the workspace there and plans as usual with the date the interrupted run used. `resume_input_changes` then applies that plan in the worktree, without a lockfile refresh, and the CLI writes the run's `--emit-decision` and `--emit-preview` files there, to get the tree a finished run leaves. Every file the plan was derived from (the manifests the loader opened, `callisto.toml`, the changesets) and every file it writes must be on disk either as the checkpoint recorded it or as that expected tree has it, compared through Git's filters, and a file the expected tree lacks counts as the run's deletion only when the index lacks it too; `HEAD`, the tags, the Callisto version and the workspace must match, and the temporary worktree directory the plan came from must hold this workspace's tree in the checkpoint, so a plan made in another directory is never applied. Anything else refuses with E340, whose help names the way out: delete the checkpoint ref and follow the E121 steps. Only then is the plan applied to the real tree. A dry run has no permit to apply in the worktree, so it reports the plan without this check. The apply's preflight and workspace resolution run before the checkpoint is created (`apply::validate_plan`), so a run that cannot start leaves no checkpoint, and a plan that writes nothing records none. The checkpoint's temporary index starts from a copy of the real one and adds the working tree tolerating unreadable files; the scratch checkout runs none of the user's hooks.
- E121 still guards states no checkpoint recorded.

- Each `PlannedBump` carries `from` and `to`. Before writing a manifest (or a platform manifest), apply reads its current version: `from` means write, `to` means already done, anything else is `UnexpectedManifestVersion`.
- A manifest already at `to` is still staged: the crashed run may have written it without `git add`.
- Apply refreshes affected lockfiles and stages generated version state before consuming changesets or exiting `pre.json`. It stages input deletions with `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch` before removing the files from disk, so a failed index update leaves the inputs available for recovery. With no checkpoint (a state another tool or an older Callisto left), E121 directs the user to inspect both diffs and finish consuming retained inputs only when the staged outputs are verified.
- A Cargo member that inherits its version (`version.workspace = true`) is pinned to a literal version when it is bumped, and `[workspace.package]` is never written, so a member that still inherits keeps the shared version. A bump of every member of a fixed group pins each of them.
- `ApplyOutcome::staged` lists every path apply staged.

## Command boundary and known gaps

`version --emit-decision` derives and validates the decision before writes, applies the plan, and writes the decision only after apply succeeds. The decision file is not wrapped in the stdout report envelope. `--emit-preview` follows the same rules: it is refused with `--dry-run`, built only from a plan without errors, and written after apply succeeds. A relative path for `--emit-decision` is relative to the workspace root, because it names a committed repository file, and a path that leaves the workspace is refused with E225 or E226 (exit 2) before anything is written; every other file flag (`--emit-preview`, `compose-pr-body --preview`, and the hidden `release` and `release-pr` flags `--intent`, `--receipt`, `--out`, `--artifact-dir`, `--input`, `--artifact-manifest`, `--source-root`) is relative to `--cwd`, like `git -C`. An absolute path is used as given.

Outside `mode: pre`, `check_partial_run` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's effective version differs from `HEAD` while a changeset remains in `HEAD` or in the working tree (including untracked files), or when a canonical manifest with an effective staged version change is present in the index. Staged metadata-only edits are allowed. During `mode: exit`, prerelease versions awaiting stable finalization remain eligible, but changed stable versions are not exempt from the retry guard. Apply retains changesets and pre-state deletion inputs until lock refresh and staging of generated state succeed, then stages their removal before unlinking them from disk. A late `--emit-decision` or `--emit-preview` write failure leaves the checkpoint in place, so running `version` again writes them.
